title: Second largest
prompt:
Write second_largest(numbers) that returns the second largest DIFFERENT value, or None if there are fewer than two different values.
Example: [4, 9, 9, 2] -> 4, because the largest is 9.
hints: Imagine a podium: first and second place. If two people tie for first, who is second?
Duplicates of the largest value must not count as the second largest. How can you get rid of repeated values first?
Plan: collect the distinct values; if fewer than 2, return None; otherwise take away the biggest one and the biggest of what's left is the answer.

edge_hints.duplicates: If the biggest value appears twice, the second largest is still a smaller, different value. Work with distinct values.
edge_hints.all-same: If all values are the same there is no second largest; the exercise says what to return.
edge_hints.single: One number has no second largest.
